name: Julia Thiele-Schuerhoff
current_role: Member of the Supervisory Board, Knorr-Bremse AG; Chair of the Executive Board, Knorr-Bremse Global Care e.V.
profile: German lawyer and heiress of Heinz Hermann Thiele (d. 2021), who built rail/truck braking maker Knorr-Bremse and held stakes in Vossloh and Lufthansa. She has sat on Knorr-Bremse's supervisory board since 2016 and leads the company-affiliated charity Knorr-Bremse Global Care.
interesting_fact: She cofounded Knorr-Bremse Global Care in 2005 after the Indian Ocean tsunami; it funds partner projects worldwide in education, emergency relief and water/sanitation/hygiene.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the board she worked inside the company as a lawyer: an LMU Munich law graduate, she was a Knorr-Bremse in-house legal adviser from 2002 to 2008. Before the 2018 Frankfurt IPO, she and her father were Knorr-Bremse's sole owners.
notes: The Thiele family has long avoided publicity. The best route is Knorr-Bremse corporate communications (those contacts are for journalists only), or via Knorr-Bremse Global Care.

name: Mette Brunsborg
current_role: Board member, Lars Larsen Group A/S (owner of JYSK) and Lars Larsens JYSK Fond
profile: Daughter of JYSK founder Lars Larsen (d. 2019). She and her brother Jacob Brunsborg (chairman) control Lars Larsen Group, the Silkeborg holding company that owns the JYSK home-furnishings chain plus BOLIA, ILVA, SOFACOMPANY and other investments. She joined the family foundation's board in 2019, taking her mother Kris Brunsborg's seat.
interesting_fact: When she joined the board of Lars Larsens JYSK Fond in 2019, she took the seat of her mother, Kris Brunsborg. The foundation's first gift under the new board was DKK 1m to Børns Vilkår to help children whose parents have mental illness.
deep_cut_fact: Away from the boardroom she runs her own farm (driver sit eget landbrug), according to the Danish encyclopedia Lex.
notes: Very private, with almost no public profile. Brother Jacob Brunsborg is the family's public face. In July 2026 Lars Larsen Group announced a new renewable-energy agreement, which could be an angle for an energy podcast. Best route is Lars Larsen Group press.

name: Wang Qicheng
current_role: Founder of the Hakim (Handing / 汉鼎) group; private investor based in Hangzhou
profile: Hangzhou entrepreneur born in the 1980s, who shares the Hurun listing with Wu Yan. While at Zhejiang University he founded Handing (Hakim) Information Technology, a smart-city systems integrator that listed on ChiNext in 2012. In 2019 he passed control of the listed company (later Haixia Innovation) to Pingtan state capital, and he now invests his own money across a portfolio of roughly 100 startups.
interesting_fact: He was an early backer of US EV maker Fisker, investing in 2017 for a stake of about 10%, and of Aurora Mobile (极光), which listed on Nasdaq in 2018. In 2020 he was named one of China's top five angel investors, the only one born in the 1980s.
deep_cut_fact: He started his company straight out of Zhejiang University's business administration department in 2003. When it listed on ChiNext nine years later, the 31-year-old was reported to be the youngest controlling shareholder of any A-share company at the time.
notes: Sources are mostly promotional Chinese articles, so verify before quoting. No personal channels are published. Hurun lists him together with Wu Yan. He has little English-language presence.

name: Jacques D'Amours
current_role: Co-founder and major shareholder (about 6%), Alimentation Couche-Tard; retired from the board in 2023
profile: Montreal-based co-founder of Alimentation Couche-Tard (Circle K), which started from one Quebec convenience store in 1980 and grew through acquisitions into a global chain of more than 17,000 stores. He worked at the company for 34 years, retiring as VP of administration in 2014, and left the board in 2023. He remains its second-largest shareholder.
interesting_fact: He was the youngest of Couche-Tard's four co-founders, alongside Alain Bouchard, Richard Fortin and Réal Plourde, and has been a billionaire since 2005.
deep_cut_fact: In the mid-1980s, aged about 28, he ran operations with Réal Plourde in Couche-Tard's small early office. The company's very first employee remembered him as 'more of an introvert' than his co-founders. His roles over the years included manager of technical services and VP of sales.
notes: Low-profile and retired from the company. Couche-Tard media relations may forward a request but does not represent him personally. Co-founder Alain Bouchard is the public face.

name: Anthony Langley
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Langley Holdings plc (Bergen Engines, Piller Power Systems, Marelli Motori, Clarke Chapman)
profile: Tony Langley founded Langley Holdings in 1975, aged 20, from the remains of his grandfather's failed engineering firm. He started by selling mining equipment to the UK coal industry, then built a group of 90+ subsidiaries through acquisitions such as Clarke Chapman (2000) and Bergen Engines (2021), both bought from Rolls-Royce. He is now repositioning the group as a supplier of grid-free, behind-the-meter power for AI data centers.
interesting_fact: Bergen Engines won its first independent power order for a new US AI data center in 2025: gas engines of 11.2MW each for E-Finity Distributed Generation. In May 2026 it won more than 500MW of orders from Liberty Energy. Langley says the group 'is now principally a power equipment supplier.'
deep_cut_fact: His Gladiator team won the 2024 Rolex TP52 World Championship in Newport, RI, the first British-flagged team to take that title and his first world title as an owner. Langley called tactics after handing the helm to two-time world champion Guillermo Parada so he could learn from him.
notes: A highly relevant guest for a data-center/energy podcast. He has given trade-press interviews (Capacity, June 2026) and attends Datacloud Global Congress in Cannes with his sons. LinkedIn is the company page, not a personal profile.

name: Stephen Lansdown
current_role: Owner, Bristol Sport (Bristol City FC, Bristol Bears, Bristol Flyers); private investor based in Guernsey
profile: Bristol-born accountant (b. 1952) who co-founded Hargreaves Lansdown with Peter Hargreaves in 1981. It grew into the UK's largest retail investment platform. He left its board in 2012 and moved to Guernsey in 2010, and now concentrates on Bristol Sport and private and impact investments. He co-founded the sustainable PE firm Earth Capital in 2008; it closed in 2024.
interesting_fact: Trained as an accountant, he started Hargreaves Lansdown trading from a bedroom in 1981. He later sold Hargreaves Lansdown shares to help fund Bristol City's redevelopment of Ashton Gate, and rescued Bristol Rugby (now Bristol Bears) when it was close to going under.
deep_cut_fact: He was an early convert to sustainable investing. In 2019 he said he had narrowed his focus to four themes: food security, energy security, clean water and waste management. Earth Capital scored every deal on its own 'Earth Dividend' ESG scorecard, mapped to the UN SDGs.
notes: He received a CBE in 2017. His energy-security and sustainability investing is a natural podcast angle. Bristol Sport is the most direct published route.
